instruction: Disable ctrl+b for toggling the sidebar in VS Code.

metadata.explanation: Task requires disabling the Ctrl+B keybinding for toggling sidebar visibility in VS Code. The evaluator checks if the keybindings.json file contains the expected entry with command '-workbench.action.toggleSidebarVisibility'. This maintains the same difficulty level as the original task.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic correctly verifies the instruction: checks if keybindings.json contains the disabling entry for ctrl+b
Expected value is semantically correct: command '-workbench.action.toggleSidebarVisibility' correctly represents disabling the keybinding (VS Code uses '-' prefix to disable)
Complete coverage: verifies the exact requirement (disable ctrl+b for sidebar toggle)
Getter extracts correct state: fetches the right file (/home/user/.config/Code/User/keybindings.json)
Metric comparison logic is correct: checks if expected keybinding dict exists in JSON array
Minor robustness issue: metric doesn't explicitly handle None from getter (would crash on file open), but this doesn't affect semantic correctness of verification logic
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add None check at start of check_json_keybindings: 'if not actual: return 0.0' before trying to open file
This would handle cases where get_vm_file fails and returns None, preventing runtime crashes

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_json_keybindings first parameter type (str) may not match getter get_vm_file return type (Union)
metric check_json_keybindings second parameter type (str) may not match expected.rules type (Dict)
